sections.h2: Exam Technique for This Essay
paras: Good essays are planned before they are written, and this topic is no exception. Spend the first five minutes making a short outline on the rough-work page: introduction, three or four body points in a sensible order, and a conclusion. This small habit prevents repetition, keeps your ideas in order, and helps you finish on time. In the examination hall, write neatly, leave a clear space between paragraphs, and check your spelling at the end if time allows. A clean, well-organised answer always scores better than a longer, confused one, even when both students know the same facts.

Practise by writing this essay once at home without looking at your notes, then compare your draft with the outline in this article and improve the weak paragraphs. Learn five or six useful words for this topic and use them naturally, not forced into every sentence. Avoid copying long sentences you do not understand, because examiners reward clear, original English. Read your essay aloud once before submitting it in practice: if a sentence sounds strange when spoken, rewrite it in simpler words. With one careful practice essay a week, your speed, confidence and marks will all improve steadily.
bullets: Write the outline first, then the essay
One main idea in every paragraph
Use specific details, not empty praise
Keep sentences short and clear
Revise spelling and full stops at the end

points: A strong opening, a clear outline and one idea per paragraph.
Specific details about teachers, library and games make the essay believable.
The model essay above can be rewritten in your own words for practice.
Good vocabulary should be used naturally, not forced.
Regular practice, not memorisation, builds essay-writing skill.

faqs.q: How do I start an essay on My School?
faqs.a: Begin with a simple personal sentence, such as naming your school and saying why you like it, then add one detail about the morning or the building. Avoid starting with a dictionary definition or a very general sentence about education. A personal, honest opening immediately makes your essay feel real.

faqs.q: What if my school is small and has few facilities?
faqs.a: Write honestly about what your school does have: good teachers, kind friends, a clean classroom or a small library. Examiners do not mark the size of your school; they mark your English, your organisation and your ideas. A sincere essay about a small school can score higher than an exaggerated essay about a large one.

faqs.q: How long should this essay be in the examination?
faqs.a: For Classes 9 and 10, about 250 to 300 words is a safe length. That is usually five to seven paragraphs: one introduction, three or four body paragraphs and one conclusion. Quality matters more than length, so do not pad your essay with repeated sentences just to make it longer.

faqs.q: Can I change the model essay in my own words?
faqs.a: Yes, and you should. Use the model essay as a guide for structure and ideas, then rewrite it in your own simple English. Examiners reward original writing, so keep the outline, change the examples where you can, and add one personal observation from your own life. You can find more study guides on the [blog](/blog/) page.

title: English Essay: Importance of Education
desc: A complete model essay on the Importance of Education with quotations, examples, outline and exam technique for Class 9-10 students.
intro: The english essay importance education topic appears in almost every board examination, because education is the foundation of personal success and national progress. Education is often called light because it removes the darkness of ignorance, just as a lamp removes darkness from a room. This article gives you a clear outline, a full model essay with quotations and examples, and practical exam tips. Before writing, you may also read the [Solved Notes](/solved.html) page and browse the [books](/books.html) section for related study material.

sections.h2: Why Education Is Called Light
paras: An uneducated person may work hard all his life, yet without knowledge he cannot understand his rights, protect his health or help his children make good decisions. Education teaches us to read, to think and to judge right from wrong, and these three powers change a person's whole life. An educated farmer uses better methods, an educated mother cares better for her children, and an educated citizen votes wisely and obeys the law. This is why education is not a luxury for the rich; it is a necessity for every child, boy or girl.

Education also builds character alongside knowledge. A truly educated person is honest, tolerant and respectful, because schooling teaches patience, cooperation and responsibility every day. When millions of citizens are educated, the whole nation benefits: there is less poverty, better health, more honest work and stronger unity. For this reason, nations that invest in schools and teachers rise faster than nations that neglect them, and every rupee spent on education returns many times over in progress and peace.
bullets: Knowledge removes ignorance
Education teaches rights and duties
Educated citizens build a strong nation
Education improves health and income
Education must reach every child

sections.h2: Essay Outline: Importance of Education
paras: A strong outline for this essay moves from the individual to the nation. Start with the meaning of education and the famous comparison with light. Then explain its benefits for the individual: knowledge, employment and character. Next, explain its benefits for society: progress, health and unity. Add one paragraph on the duty of parents, teachers and government to spread education. End with a conclusion that calls on every student to value schooling and work hard.

Quotations strengthen this essay, but use only one or two short ones that you remember correctly. A famous saying is that knowledge is power, and another is that education is the most powerful weapon to change the world. Place a quotation in the introduction or the conclusion, never in every paragraph, and explain it in your own words afterwards. An unexplained quotation looks copied; an explained one looks thoughtful.
bullets: Introduction: education as light, quotation
Body 1: benefits for the individual
Body 2: benefits for society and the nation
Body 3: duty to spread education to all
Conclusion: value education and work hard

sections.h2: Model Essay: Importance of Education
paras: Education is the light that removes the darkness of ignorance from human life, and without it a person cannot see the path to success. It is said that knowledge is power, and this saying is completely true, because knowledge gives a person confidence, employment and respect in society. An educated person can read books, understand the world, solve problems and take wise decisions, while an uneducated person depends on others even for small daily matters. Education therefore begins in childhood and continues throughout life, and every student should treat it as a precious treasure.

Education benefits the individual in many ways. It opens the door to good jobs, because doctors, engineers, teachers and officers all reach their positions through years of study. It also improves health, because educated people understand cleanliness, balanced food and the importance of visiting a doctor on time. Above all, education builds character: it teaches honesty, patience, tolerance and respect for others, and a person with good character is respected even more than a person with great wealth. A degree without character is incomplete, and true education always joins knowledge with good manners.

sections.h2: Model Essay: Conclusion and Useful Vocabulary
paras: Education also benefits the whole nation. When citizens are educated, they work honestly, pay taxes, obey laws and take part in the progress of the country. Educated mothers raise healthier and better-educated children, educated farmers increase production, and educated workers run industries with skill. On the other hand, ignorance breeds poverty, superstition and quarrels, and no nation can progress while its people remain uneducated. For this reason, parents must send every child to school, teachers must teach with sincerity, and the government must provide books, buildings and trained teachers in every village and town.

In conclusion, education is the greatest wealth a person can possess, because wealth can be stolen but knowledge can never be taken away. I am grateful for the chance to study, and I promise to work hard, respect my teachers and use my education for the good of my family and my country. Every student who values education today will become a useful citizen tomorrow, and every nation that educates its children secures its own bright future.
bullets: ignorance — lack of knowledge
treasure — something very precious
character — moral qualities of a person
superstition — belief without reason or proof
progress — steady improvement towards a better state

sections.h2: Exam Technique for This Essay
paras: Good essays are planned before they are written, and this topic is no exception. Spend the first five minutes making a short outline on the rough-work page: introduction, three or four body points in a sensible order, and a conclusion. This small habit prevents repetition, keeps your ideas in order, and helps you finish on time. In the examination hall, write neatly, leave a clear space between paragraphs, and check your spelling at the end if time allows. A clean, well-organised answer always scores better than a longer, confused one, even when both students know the same facts.

Practise by writing this essay once at home without looking at your notes, then compare your draft with the outline in this article and improve the weak paragraphs. Learn five or six useful words for this topic and use them naturally, not forced into every sentence. Avoid copying long sentences you do not understand, because examiners reward clear, original English. Read your essay aloud once before submitting it in practice: if a sentence sounds strange when spoken, rewrite it in simpler words. With one careful practice essay a week, your speed, confidence and marks will all improve steadily.
bullets: Use one short quotation, explained in your own words
Move from individual benefits to national benefits
Give concrete examples: farmer, mother, worker
End with a personal promise or call to action
Avoid repeating the word important in every sentence

points: Education is light because it removes ignorance and guides decisions.
Individual benefits include jobs, health and character.
National benefits include progress, unity and honest citizenship.
One well-explained quotation is stronger than three copied ones.
Spreading education to every child is a shared duty.

faqs.q: Which quotation can I safely use in this essay?
faqs.a: Use a short, famous one you remember correctly, such as knowledge is power. Write it in your own sentence and explain what it means for a student. Never invent a quotation or attribute a saying to a famous person if you are not sure who said it.

faqs.q: How do I avoid repeating the same point in this essay?
faqs.a: Give each paragraph a different job: one for the individual, one for the nation and one for the duty to spread education. If two sentences say the same thing, delete the weaker one and replace it with an example instead.

faqs.q: How long should this essay be in the examination?
faqs.a: For Classes 9 and 10, about 250 to 300 words is a safe length. That is usually five to seven paragraphs: one introduction, three or four body paragraphs and one conclusion. Quality matters more than length, so do not pad your essay with repeated sentences just to make it longer.

faqs.q: Can I change the model essay in my own words?
faqs.a: Yes, and you should. Use the model essay as a guide for structure and ideas, then rewrite it in your own simple English. Examiners reward original writing, so keep the outline, change the examples where you can, and add one personal observation from your own life. title: English Essay: Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah
desc: A complete model essay on Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah with his life, leadership, lessons and exam technique for Class 9-10.
intro: The english essay quaid e azam topic is one of the most respected essay topics in Pakistan, because the Founder of the Nation is a model of honesty, hard work and determination. Muhammad Ali Jinnah was born on 25 December 1876 in Karachi, became a great lawyer and leader, and led the Muslims of the subcontinent to the creation of Pakistan on 14 August 1947. This article gives you an outline, a full model essay and exam tips, so that you can write about his life with respect and accuracy. Related notes are available on the [Solved Notes](/solved.html) page and in the [books](/books.html) collection.

sections.h2: Why the Quaid-e-Azam Still Inspires Us
paras: Great leaders are remembered not for wealth or power, but for character, and the Quaid-e-Azam possessed character in the highest degree. He was honest in his dealings, punctual in his habits, firm in his principles and fearless in speaking the truth. He never accepted a bribe, never broke his word and never changed his stand for personal gain. Students can learn from him that success comes from discipline and hard work, not from shortcuts, and that a single honest person can change the history of a whole nation.

His greatest achievement was Pakistan, a separate homeland where Muslims could live according to their faith, laws and culture. He achieved this not by violence, but by constitutional struggle, powerful speeches and unshakable unity of the Muslim League. His guiding motto, Faith, Unity and Discipline, remains the best advice for every Pakistani student today. Faith gives courage, unity gives strength, and discipline gives success, and any student who practises these three qualities can achieve great things in life.
bullets: Born 25 December 1876 in Karachi
Became a brilliant lawyer and leader
Led the struggle for Pakistan
Pakistan came into being on 14 August 1947
Motto: Faith, Unity and Discipline

sections.h2: Essay Outline: Quaid-e-Azam
paras: Arrange this essay in time order: birth and early life, education and legal career, political struggle, achievement of Pakistan, and lessons for students. Time order is easy to follow and prevents confusion, which is important when an essay covers a whole life. Keep dates short and only those you are sure of: birth year 1876 and independence year 1947 are the two essential dates. Do not guess at other dates or events; a wrong date in a history essay damages your credibility.

The conclusion should not repeat the biography; it should explain what we must learn. Write about honesty, hard work, unity and discipline, and end with a promise to follow his example in student life. This turns a simple life story into a meaningful essay with a message, which is exactly what examiners look for in a personality essay.
bullets: Introduction: the Founder of Pakistan
Body 1: early life and education
Body 2: legal career and leadership
Body 3: struggle and creation of Pakistan
Conclusion: lessons for students today

sections.h2: Model Essay: Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah
paras: Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah is the Founder of Pakistan, and every Pakistani remembers him with love, respect and gratitude. He was born on 25 December 1876 in Karachi, and from his childhood he was serious, hardworking and fond of reading. After completing his early education, he went to England to study law, and on his return he became one of the most brilliant lawyers of Bombay. His honesty was famous: he never took a case he believed to be unjust, and even his opponents admired his truthfulness and dignity.

In politics, the Quaid first worked for Hindu-Muslim unity, but when he saw that Muslims would not get justice and freedom in a united India, he led the demand for a separate homeland. With wisdom, patience and powerful arguments, he united the Muslims of the subcontinent under the flag of the Muslim League. He faced opposition, illness and great difficulties, yet he never lost courage and never compromised on principles. At last, on 14 August 1947, his dream came true and Pakistan appeared on the map of the world, and the nation gave him the title of Quaid-e-Azam, the Great Leader.

sections.h2: Model Essay: Conclusion and Useful Vocabulary
paras: The Quaid-e-Azam died on 11 September 1948, only a year after independence, but his work and his message live on. He gave us the motto of Faith, Unity and Discipline, and this motto is a complete guide for national life. Faith means trust in our cause and in ourselves; unity means standing together beyond province, language and sect; discipline means obeying laws and doing our duty honestly. If students follow this motto, they will succeed in examinations and in life, and Pakistan will progress towards the bright future its Founder dreamed of.

Useful vocabulary for this essay includes: founder for the person who establishes something, determination for firm decision, constitutional for done through law and peaceful methods, and gratitude for thankfulness. Use the title Quaid-e-Azam with respect and spell Muhammad Ali Jinnah correctly, as examiners notice errors in famous names. Avoid exaggeration: the Quaid's real life is inspiring enough without invented stories, so write only facts you know.

determination — firmness of purpose
constitutional — through law, not violence
opponent — a person who disagrees or competes
gratitude — deep thankfulness

title: English Essay: Science in Daily Life
desc: A complete model essay on Science in Daily Life with examples from kitchen to mobile phone, outline and exam tips for Class 9-10.
intro: The english essay science daily life topic is easy to write well, because science surrounds you from the moment you wake up until you sleep. The alarm clock, the electric light, the gas stove, the mobile phone and the medicine in your home are all gifts of science. This article gives you an outline, a full model essay and exam tips, so that you can turn everyday examples into a strong, well-organised essay. You can find more study material on the [Solved Notes](/solved.html) page and in the [books](/books.html) section.

sections.h2: Science Is Not Only in the Laboratory
paras: Many students think science lives only in textbooks and laboratories, but in truth science lives in every room of the house. When you switch on a fan, you use electricity; when you cook food on a stove, you use heat energy; when you keep milk fresh in a refrigerator, you use the science of cooling. Even the soap that cleans your hands and the toothpaste that protects your teeth are products of chemistry. Once you notice these examples, you will never run out of ideas for this essay.

Science has also changed travel, communication and medicine beyond recognition. A journey that once took weeks now takes hours by aeroplane, and a message that once took days now reaches another country in seconds through a mobile phone. Doctors use X-rays, vaccinations and modern medicines to cure diseases that once killed thousands of people. At the same time, science must be used wisely, because the same knowledge that makes electricity can also make weapons, and the same factories that make goods can pollute the air if they are careless.
bullets: Morning: alarm, light, toothpaste, breakfast
Kitchen: stove, refrigerator, clean water
Communication: mobile phone, television, internet
Health: medicines, vaccination, hospitals
Travel: bus, train, aeroplane

sections.h2: Essay Outline: Science in Daily Life
paras: The best structure for this essay follows your own day: morning, kitchen, communication, health and travel, ending with a balanced conclusion. This day-order structure is natural, easy to remember and full of examples, so you will not need to memorise abstract points. Start with a general introduction about science as a servant of humanity, then walk through the day giving one or two examples in each paragraph. End by saying that science is a good servant but a bad master, and must be used for peace and human welfare.

Make sure every example is real and from daily life, not from a science fiction film. Examiners reward the student who writes about a refrigerator and a mobile phone more than the student who writes vaguely about wonderful inventions. Name the object, say what it does, and say how life would be difficult without it. That three-step pattern — object, use, benefit — makes every paragraph strong.
bullets: Introduction: science as a servant of humanity
Body 1: morning and home
Body 2: kitchen and food
Body 3: communication and travel
Body 4: health and medicine
Conclusion: use science wisely for welfare

sections.h2: Model Essay: Science in Daily Life
paras: Science plays a very important part in our daily life, and it is difficult to imagine even a single day without its blessings. In the morning, the alarm clock wakes us, the electric bulb removes darkness, and the tap gives us clean water for washing and drinking. At breakfast, science helps us again: the stove cooks our food quickly, the refrigerator keeps milk and vegetables fresh, and the toaster prepares bread in minutes. Without science, our mornings would be slow, dark and full of hard labour, but with science they are easy, comfortable and pleasant.

Science has also made communication and travel wonderfully easy. Through the mobile phone we can talk to a relative in another city or country in seconds, and through television and the internet we learn the news of the whole world while sitting at home. Buses, trains and aeroplanes carry us quickly and safely over long distances, and students can now study from books, videos and online lessons that were unknown to their grandparents. In the field of health, science has given us medicines, vaccinations, X-rays and modern hospitals, so diseases that once caused great fear can now be treated and often cured completely.

sections.h2: Model Essay: Conclusion and Useful Vocabulary
paras: However, we must remember that science is a good servant but a bad master, and it must be used with wisdom and care. The same science that produces electricity and medicines can also produce harmful weapons and pollution if people use it selfishly. Factories must control their smoke, drivers must avoid unnecessary horns and smoke, and students must use mobile phones for learning rather than wasting hours on useless games. In conclusion, science has made our life comfortable, healthy and fast, and if we use it honestly for the welfare of humanity, it will continue to be our greatest blessing.

Useful vocabulary includes: invention for a new device or method, blessing for a great benefit, vaccination for protection against disease, and welfare for the health and happiness of people. Use verbs actively: science cooks, preserves, connects and cures. Avoid writing science has made our life easy in every paragraph; vary your sentences by giving a new example each time, so the essay stays fresh from beginning to end.

blessing — a great benefit or gift
vaccination — protection against a disease
welfare — health, happiness and safety
labour — hard physical work

title: English Essay: My Favourite Book
desc: A complete model essay on My Favourite Book with personal reasons, outline, vocabulary and exam technique for Class 9-10 students.
intro: The english essay favourite book topic asks for something personal: not a summary of a story, but the reasons why one book matters to you. Examiners love this topic because it separates memorised essays from honest ones, and the best essays sound like a real student talking about a real book. This article gives you an outline, a full model essay and exam tips, so you can write sincerely about a book you truly enjoyed. More study help is on the [Solved Notes](/solved.html) page and in the [books](/books.html) collection.

sections.h2: What Makes a Book a Favourite?
paras: A favourite book is not necessarily the longest or most famous book; it is the book you return to again and again because it teaches you something or makes you feel something. It may be a book of stories, a biography of a great person, or a book about science and nature. What matters is that you can explain why you like it: the characters feel real, the language is beautiful, or the lessons help you in daily life. An essay that says I like this book because it is interesting, without giving reasons, will always score low.

Before writing, ask yourself three questions about your book. First, what is the book about in two sentences? Second, which part or character impressed you most, and why? Third, what did you learn from it that changed your thinking or behaviour? Your answers to these three questions become the three body paragraphs of your essay, and suddenly the essay writes itself. Honesty is your greatest strength here: write about a book you have actually read, even if it is simple, rather than pretending to love a difficult book you never opened.
bullets: Name of the book and its author
What the book is about, briefly
Your favourite character or part
Lessons you learned from it
Why you recommend it to friends

sections.h2: Essay Outline: My Favourite Book
paras: Structure this essay as introduction, summary, favourite part, lessons, and recommendation. The introduction names the book and says how you found it, perhaps as a gift or from the school library. The summary paragraph must be short, only three or four sentences, because the essay is about your feelings, not a retelling of the whole story. The next two paragraphs carry the real marks: your favourite part with reasons, and the lessons you learned. End by recommending the book to other students and saying why they would enjoy it too.

Do not retell the entire story chapter by chapter, and do not reveal the ending in full detail if it would spoil the book for the reader. A good book essay is like a recommendation to a friend: enough detail to create interest, plus honest personal reasons. Use phrases such as I was impressed by, I learned that, and I recommend this book because, which naturally produce the personal voice examiners want.
bullets: Introduction: name, author, how you found it
Body 1: short summary in a few sentences
Body 2: favourite character or part, with reasons
Body 3: lessons learned and change in you
Conclusion: recommendation to other students

sections.h2: Model Essay: My Favourite Book
paras: My favourite book is a small book of inspiring stories and biographies that my teacher gave me as a prize, and I have read it many times with great pleasure. It contains short, simple stories about honest, brave and hardworking people who faced difficulties with patience and never gave up. The language is easy, the stories are short, and every story ends with a lesson that a student can understand and apply in daily life. I keep this book on my study table, and whenever I feel tired or disappointed, I open it at any page and find new courage.

The part I like most is the story of a poor student who studied under a street light because his home had no electricity, yet he worked so hard that he became a successful teacher. This story impressed me deeply, because it taught me that excuses never help and hard work always pays in the end. I often think of that student when I feel lazy about homework, and his example pushes me to open my books again. The book also teaches honesty, kindness to others and respect for parents and teachers, and these lessons are more valuable than any examination marks.

sections.h2: Model Essay: Conclusion and Useful Vocabulary
paras: This book has changed my thinking in a real way. Before reading it, I believed that success depended on wealth and luck, but now I understand that patience, discipline and sincere effort matter far more. I have started managing my time better, helping my younger brother with his lessons, and speaking politely even when I disagree with someone. In conclusion, I recommend this book to every student, because it is short, interesting and full of lessons for life. A good book is a true friend, and this book has become one of my best friends, guiding me quietly every day.

Useful vocabulary includes: biography for the life story of a person, character for a person in a story, impressed for deeply affected, and recommend for advising others to read something. Use the present tense when describing what the book teaches, and the past tense when retelling a story event. Avoid copying long quotations from the book; one short sentence, explained in your own words, is enough and sounds more honest.

character — a person in a story
impressed — deeply affected in a good way
recommend — advise others to try something
inspiring — giving courage and hope

title: English Essay: Pollution and Its Solution
desc: A complete model essay on Pollution and Its Solution covering air, water and land pollution with practical fixes for Class 9-10.
intro: The english essay pollution topic matters to every student in Pakistan, because polluted air, dirty water and littered streets affect our health every day. Pollution means adding harmful substances to the environment, and its solution begins with understanding its three main kinds: air, water and land pollution. This article gives you an outline, a full model essay and exam tips. You can also find study material on the [Solved Notes](/solved.html) page and in the [books](/books.html) section.

sections.h2: Three Kinds of Pollution
paras: Air pollution comes from smoke of vehicles, factories and burning rubbish, and it causes cough, asthma and other chest diseases, especially in crowded cities. Water pollution comes from sewage, factory waste and plastic thrown into rivers and canals, and it spreads stomach diseases and kills fish and plants. Land pollution comes from plastic bags, garbage and chemicals dumped on open ground, which spoil soil, block drains and breed flies and mosquitoes. When you understand these three kinds separately, your essay becomes organised and easy to follow.

The causes of pollution are mostly human activities, which is good news, because human activities can also be changed. People burn rubbish instead of disposing of it properly, factories release smoke without filters, and shoppers use plastic bags for every small purchase. Floods worsen when drains are blocked by plastic, and dirty water spreads disease when sewage mixes with drinking water. Every cause in your essay should be paired with a solution, because an essay that only complains, without suggesting fixes, feels incomplete to an examiner.
bullets: Air: vehicle and factory smoke
Water: sewage, factory waste, plastic
Land: garbage, plastic bags, chemicals
Effects: cough, stomach disease, blocked drains
Solutions: trees, filters, clean habits

sections.h2: Essay Outline: Pollution and Its Solution
paras: Use a clear problem-and-solution structure: introduction, air pollution, water and land pollution, solutions, and conclusion. Give each kind of pollution its own paragraph with causes and effects, then devote a full paragraph to practical solutions that students and families can actually follow. Practical solutions score higher than grand promises: planting trees, using dustbins, avoiding plastic bags, saving water and keeping streets clean are all actions a student can describe honestly.

End with a shared responsibility message: government, factories and citizens must all play their part. Government can enforce laws and provide dustbins and clean water, factories can install filters, and citizens can stop littering and plant trees. When all three work together, the environment improves quickly. Avoid blaming one group only, and avoid inventing statistics; write about effects you can explain, such as cough from smoke or disease from dirty water.
bullets: Introduction: meaning of pollution
Body 1: air pollution, causes and effects
Body 2: water and land pollution
Body 3: practical solutions for all
Conclusion: shared responsibility, clean future

diagram.caption: Essay Structure: Pollution and Its Solution. Follow this order when you write your essay in the examination hall.

sections.h2: Model Essay: Pollution and Its Solution
paras: Pollution is one of the greatest problems of the modern world, and it means making our air, water and land dirty and harmful through human activities. Air pollution is caused by the smoke of vehicles, factories and burning rubbish, and it fills our cities with dust and poisonous gases. People who breathe this polluted air suffer from cough, asthma and other diseases of the chest, and children and old people suffer the most. Water pollution is equally dangerous: sewage, factory waste and plastic are thrown into rivers and canals, so drinking water becomes unsafe and fish and crops are harmed. Land pollution spoils our streets and fields, because garbage and plastic bags block drains, breed mosquitoes and make our surroundings ugly and unhealthy.

The solution to pollution begins with simple habits that every student and family can adopt today. We must plant more trees, because trees clean the air, give shade and make our surroundings beautiful. We must use dustbins instead of throwing rubbish on streets, carry cloth bags instead of plastic bags, and save water instead of wasting it. Factories must install filters to clean their smoke, and the government must enforce laws against dumping waste into rivers and provide proper dustbins and clean drinking water in every area. Schools can help by teaching students about cleanliness and by organising tree-planting and cleanliness campaigns every year.

sections.h2: Model Essay: Conclusion and Useful Vocabulary
paras: In conclusion, pollution is a problem created by human beings, and therefore human beings can solve it if they act together with sincerity. If every citizen stops littering, plants even one tree and uses water carefully, our cities will become cleaner within a few years. A clean environment means healthy children, fresh air, safe water and a beautiful country, and these blessings are worth far more than the small effort they require. Let us promise today to keep our homes, streets and schools clean, because a clean Pakistan is the duty and the pride of every Pakistani.

Useful vocabulary includes: environment for our surroundings, sewage for dirty waste water, filter for a device that cleans smoke or water, and campaign for an organised effort for a cause. Use cause-and-effect language: smoke causes cough, plastic blocks drains, trees clean air. This language makes your essay logical and persuasive, and it shows the examiner that you understand the problem, not merely memorised a paragraph.
bullets: environment — our surroundings: air, water, land
sewage — dirty waste water from homes
filter — a device that removes harmful substances
campaign — an organised effort for a cause
breed — to produce young, as mosquitoes do

sections.h2: Exam Technique for This Essay
paras: Good essays are planned before they are written, and this topic is no exception. Spend the first five minutes making a short outline on the rough-work page: introduction, three or four body points in a sensible order, and a conclusion. This small habit prevents repetition, keeps your ideas in order, and helps you finish on time. In the examination hall, write neatly, leave a clear space between paragraphs, and check your spelling at the end if time allows. A clean, well-organised answer always scores better than a longer, confused one, even when both students know the same facts.

Practise by writing this essay once at home without looking at your notes, then compare your draft with the outline in this article and improve the weak paragraphs. Learn five or six useful words for this topic and use them naturally, not forced into every sentence. Avoid copying long sentences you do not understand, because examiners reward clear, original English. Read your essay aloud once before submitting it in practice: if a sentence sounds strange when spoken, rewrite it in simpler words. With one careful practice essay a week, your speed, confidence and marks will all improve steadily.
bullets: Pair every cause with a solution
Cover air, water and land separately
Give practical solutions students can do
Avoid invented statistics and figures
End with shared responsibility, not blame alone

points: Pollution has three main kinds: air, water and land.
Human causes can be changed by human action.
Practical solutions score higher than grand promises.
Government, factories and citizens share responsibility.
A clean environment protects health and beauty.

faqs.q: How do I organise a pollution essay without repeating myself?
faqs.a: Give air, water and land each their own paragraph, and keep all solutions together in one paragraph near the end. If a sentence fits in two paragraphs, keep it in the stronger one and delete it from the other.

faqs.q: Can I write about pollution in my own city?
faqs.a: Yes, and it makes your essay stronger. Mention littered streets, smoke from traffic or blocked drains as examples, without naming or blaming any individual. Local examples show observation, which examiners reward.

faqs.q: How long should this essay be in the examination?
faqs.a: For Classes 9 and 10, about 250 to 300 words is a safe length. That is usually five to seven paragraphs: one introduction, three or four body paragraphs and one conclusion. Quality matters more than length, so do not pad your essay with repeated sentences just to make it longer.

faqs.q: Can I change the model essay in my own words?
faqs.a: Yes, and you should. Use the model essay as a guide for structure and ideas, then rewrite it in your own simple English. Examiners reward original writing, so keep the outline, change the examples where you can, and add one personal observation from your own life. You can find more study guides on the [blog](/blog/) page.

title: English Essay: Discipline in Student Life
desc: A complete model essay on Discipline in Student Life covering home, school and the exam hall, with outline and exam tips.
intro: The english essay discipline topic is a favourite of examiners because discipline is the habit that turns talent into success. Discipline means obeying rules, managing time and controlling oneself, whether at home, in school or in the examination hall. This article gives you an outline, a full model essay and exam tips, so you can write about discipline with real examples from student life. Related material is available on the [Solved Notes](/solved.html) page and in the [books](/books.html) collection.

sections.h2: Discipline Is Freedom, Not Punishment
paras: Many students think discipline means punishment, but true discipline is a gift you give yourself. A disciplined student wakes on time, completes homework before play, and enters the examination hall calm and prepared, while an undisciplined student rushes, forgets books and panics. Discipline saves time instead of wasting it: a fixed timetable for study, play, rest and prayer removes daily confusion about what to do next. Armies, sports teams, hospitals and schools all run on discipline, because no large group can succeed when everyone acts on sudden wishes.

Discipline also builds character and respect. A student who listens quietly in class, speaks politely to teachers and stands in queue without pushing shows good manners and earns the trust of others. At home, discipline means helping parents, keeping your room tidy and respecting elders. In the examination hall, it means honest work, silence and following instructions. These small daily acts, repeated for years, shape a person who can be trusted with bigger duties in adult life, and that is why teachers value discipline as much as intelligence.
bullets: Home: timetable, helping parents, respect
School: punctuality, listening, good manners
Playground: rules, fair play, teamwork
Exam hall: honesty, silence, instructions
Life: character, trust, success

sections.h2: Essay Outline: Discipline in Student Life
paras: Structure this essay by places: home, school, playground and examination hall, ending with a conclusion about success. This place-by-place structure gives you four ready paragraphs, each with its own examples, so you will not repeat yourself. Start with a definition of discipline and a short statement of its importance. Then move through home and school, where most of student life happens, before covering games and examinations. End with the message that discipline is the key to success in every field.

Use concrete verbs to make discipline visible: wake, complete, listen, queue, obey, manage. Vague essays say discipline is very important again and again; strong essays show a student waking on time, finishing homework, and sitting quietly in the examination hall. One example per paragraph is enough if it is specific and honest, and it will make your essay feel real rather than memorised.
bullets: Introduction: meaning and importance of discipline
Body 1: discipline at home
Body 2: discipline at school
Body 3: discipline in games and examinations
Conclusion: discipline as the key to success

sections.h2: Model Essay: Discipline in Student Life
paras: Discipline is the habit of obeying rules, managing time and controlling oneself, and it is the key to success in student life. A disciplined student follows a timetable: he wakes up early, offers prayers, revises lessons, goes to school on time and completes homework before play. At home, discipline means respecting parents and elders, helping in household work and keeping books and belongings in order. Such a student never wastes time in useless activities, because he knows that time lost can never be recovered, and every hour used wisely brings him closer to his goals.

At school, discipline shows itself in punctuality, attention and good manners. A disciplined student reaches school before the bell, listens to teachers quietly, stands in queue, and speaks politely to classmates and teachers. On the playground, discipline means following the rules of the game, accepting the referee's decision and playing fairly even when losing. In the examination hall, discipline means honest work, complete silence and careful obedience to instructions, because cheating may give marks once but destroys character forever. A student who practises discipline in these small matters grows into a responsible citizen whom everyone trusts.

sections.h2: Model Essay: Conclusion and Useful Vocabulary
paras: In conclusion, discipline is more valuable than talent alone, because talent without discipline is wasted, while ordinary ability with discipline achieves great results. History shows that great leaders, scientists and sportsmen all reached success through regular habits and self-control, not through sudden luck. I therefore try to follow a daily timetable, respect my teachers and elders, and work honestly in every examination. If every student adopts discipline, our schools will become peaceful, our results will improve, and our country will gain honest and hardworking citizens for its future.

Useful vocabulary includes: punctuality for being on time, timetable for a fixed plan of the day, self-control for managing one's own wishes, and citizen for a member of a country. Use the phrase key to success naturally in the introduction or conclusion, but do not repeat it in every paragraph. Pair discipline with a verb each time: practise discipline, follow discipline, maintain discipline, so your sentences stay varied and correct.

faqs.a: Punishment is imposed by others, while discipline is a habit you choose yourself. A disciplined student follows a timetable and rules willingly, not from fear. Explain this difference in your introduction to show mature thinking.

title: English Essay: Sports and Health
desc: A complete model essay on Sports and Health covering healthy body, healthy mind, teamwork and fair play for Class 9-10 students.
intro: The english essay sports health topic connects two great blessings: a strong body and a peaceful mind. The old saying, a healthy mind lives in a healthy body, reminds us that study alone is not enough; students also need games, exercise and fresh air. This article gives you an outline, a full model essay and exam tips. More study material is on the [Solved Notes](/solved.html) page and in the [books](/books.html) collection.

sections.h2: Why Students Need Sports
paras: Long hours of sitting with books tire the body and dull the mind, and sports provide the healthy break that restores both. Running, playing cricket, football or hockey, and even brisk walking strengthen muscles, improve blood circulation and build stamina. Students who play regularly fall ill less often, sleep better and return to study with fresh energy. Sports also protect students from harmful habits: a student busy with games in the evening has little time or interest for idle gossip or useless screen time.

Sports teach lessons that no textbook can teach so vividly. Team games teach cooperation, because victory requires passing, supporting and trusting teammates, not selfish play. They teach fair play, because players must accept the referee's decision and respect opponents even in defeat. They teach leadership and courage, because a captain must decide quickly and a player must try again after failure. These qualities help students in examinations, jobs and family life long after school games are over.
bullets: Body: strength, stamina, fresh energy
Mind: freshness, better sleep, less stress
Teamwork: cooperation and trust
Fair play: rules, respect, accepting defeat
Balance: study plus games, not games alone

sections.h2: Essay Outline: Sports and Health
paras: Organise this essay as body, mind, teamwork and fair play, ending with balance. Start with the famous saying about a healthy mind in a healthy body and explain it simply. Then give one paragraph to physical health, one to mental freshness, and one to teamwork and character. The conclusion must stress balance: sports should support study, not replace it, and a good student gives proper time to both books and games. This balanced ending impresses examiners, because it shows maturity rather than one-sided enthusiasm.

Name real games that students play in Pakistan, such as cricket, hockey, football and badminton, but do not turn the essay into a match report. One sentence about a game is enough; the paragraph should explain the benefit, not describe every ball or goal. Also mention simple exercise for students without a playground, such as walking, running or skipping, so your essay feels practical for every reader.
bullets: Introduction: healthy mind in a healthy body
Body 1: sports and physical health
Body 2: sports and mental freshness
Body 3: teamwork, fair play and character
Conclusion: balance between study and games

sections.h2: Model Essay: Sports and Health
paras: Sports are essential for health, because a healthy mind lives in a healthy body, and no student can study well with a weak and tired body. Games such as cricket, hockey, football and badminton strengthen our muscles, improve blood circulation and build stamina for daily work. A student who plays regularly enjoys fresh air and sunshine, eats well, sleeps soundly and falls ill less often than a student who sits all day without exercise. Sports also remove laziness: after an hour of play, the body feels active and the mind feels fresh, so homework becomes easier instead of harder.

Sports also improve the mind and character in ways that books alone cannot. Team games teach cooperation, because players must pass, support and trust one another to win, and selfish play always harms the team. They teach fair play, because a true sportsman follows the rules, respects the referee and congratulates the opponent even after defeat. They build courage and leadership, because a captain learns to decide quickly and every player learns to try again after failure. A student who learns these qualities on the playground becomes confident, patient and cooperative in the classroom and in later life as well.

sections.h2: Model Essay: Conclusion and Useful Vocabulary
paras: However, balance is necessary, because sports are meant to support study, not to replace it. A wise student gives proper time to both: he studies seriously in study hours and plays heartily in games periods and evenings, without neglecting either duty. Schools should therefore provide playgrounds, trained coaches and regular sports competitions, and parents should encourage children to play instead of spending all free time on screens. In conclusion, sports keep our body strong, our mind fresh and our character noble, and every student should play daily for a healthy, happy and successful life.

Useful vocabulary includes: stamina for lasting energy, circulation for the movement of blood in the body, opponent for the other player or team, and sportsmanship for fair and respectful behaviour in games. Use the saying about a healthy mind in a healthy body once, in the introduction or conclusion, and explain it in your own words. Avoid claiming that sports alone guarantee success; the balanced message is what makes this essay wise and complete.

circulation — movement of blood in the body
opponent — the other player or team
sportsmanship — fair, respectful behaviour in games
cooperation — working together for a shared goal

title: English Essay: My Aim in Life
desc: A complete model essay on My Aim in Life with how to choose an aim, a plan to reach it, and exam technique for Class 9-10.
intro: The english essay aim in life topic asks a personal question that every student should think about seriously: what do you want to become, and what will you do to reach that goal? A person without an aim is like a ship without a rudder, drifting wherever the wind blows, while a person with a clear aim works with purpose every day. This article gives you an outline, a full model essay and exam tips. More help is on the [Solved Notes](/solved.html) page and in the [books](/books.html) collection.

sections.h2: Why Every Student Needs an Aim
paras: An aim gives direction to study. When you know you want to become a teacher, a doctor, an engineer or a good businessman, every lesson gains meaning, because you can see how today's hard work builds tomorrow's career. Without an aim, students study only for examinations, forget lessons quickly, and waste time in confusion about the future. With an aim, even difficult subjects feel worthwhile, because the student understands that mathematics, science and English are stepping stones, not obstacles.

Choosing an aim requires honesty about your interests, abilities and circumstances. A student who loves helping others may aim to become a doctor or teacher; a student who loves building and machines may aim to become an engineer; a student who loves business may aim to become an honest trader. There is no single best aim: every honest profession serves society, and the best aim is the one that matches your talent and lets you serve others. Parents and teachers can advise, but the final choice should respect the student's own interest, because forced aims rarely lead to happiness or success.
bullets: Aim gives direction to daily study
Choose by interest, ability and service
Every honest profession is respectable
A plan turns an aim into action
Hard work, patience and honesty are required

sections.h2: Essay Outline: My Aim in Life
paras: Structure this essay as introduction, choice, plan, difficulties, and conclusion. The introduction uses the ship-without-rudder comparison and states your aim clearly. The second paragraph explains why you chose this aim: interest, talent, or a wish to serve society. The third paragraph is the plan: subjects to study, habits to build, and steps year by year. The fourth paragraph honestly admits difficulties, such as hard examinations or long study, and says how you will face them. End with a promise to work sincerely and serve your country.

In this model essay, the aim chosen is to become a teacher, because teaching is noble, respected and open to a sincere student. If your own aim is different, keep the same structure and change the second and third paragraphs to match your aim: a future doctor would mention science subjects and medical college, while a future engineer would mention mathematics and technical study. The structure works for every aim, which is why learning it once helps you in many examinations.
bullets: Introduction: aim as a rudder, state your aim
Body 1: why you chose this aim
Body 2: plan to achieve it, step by step
Body 3: difficulties and how to face them
Conclusion: promise and service to society

sections.h2: Model Essay: My Aim in Life
paras: Every person must have an aim in life, because a person without an aim is like a ship without a rudder, drifting aimlessly on the sea. My aim in life is to become a teacher, because teaching is a noble profession that builds the future of a nation. A teacher shapes the minds and character of hundreds of students, and through them serves the whole country quietly and sincerely. I have loved teaching since childhood: I enjoy explaining lessons to my younger brother, and his success gives me more happiness than my own marks. I also admire my own teachers, whose patience and kindness have inspired me to follow their path.

To achieve this aim, I have made a clear plan and I follow it with sincerity. First, I study all subjects seriously, especially English, because a teacher must express ideas clearly, and I read good books to improve my knowledge. Second, I practise explaining lessons to my friends and younger students, which improves my confidence and speaking skills. Third, I observe my teachers carefully: how they manage the class, how they explain difficult points, and how they treat every student with fairness. After completing my education, I hope to join a teacher training course and then serve in a school, preferably in my own area, where good teachers are needed most.

sections.h2: Model Essay: Conclusion and Useful Vocabulary
paras: I know that the path to my aim is not easy. I will face difficult examinations, long years of study and moments of disappointment, but I will meet them with patience, hard work and prayer. If I fail in one examination, I will try again with better preparation instead of losing courage, because success belongs to those who do not give up. In conclusion, my aim is not wealth or fame, but the honour of guiding young minds towards knowledge and good character. If I become a sincere and hardworking teacher, I will consider my life successful, and I will repay my parents, teachers and country for all they have given me.

Useful vocabulary includes: rudder for the device that steers a ship, noble for honourable and respected, profession for a career requiring training, and sincere for honest and genuine. If your aim differs, adapt the vocabulary: a doctor heals, an engineer builds, a farmer feeds, a soldier defends. Keep the plan paragraph specific: name subjects, habits and steps, because a vague plan convinces no examiner, while a step-by-step plan shows a thinking student.

title: English Essay: Role of Media in Modern Life
desc: A complete model essay on the Role of Media in Modern Life covering media as teacher, watchdog and entertainer for Class 9-10.
intro: The english essay role of media topic is highly relevant today, because television, newspapers, radio and the internet shape what millions of people know, think and discuss every day. Media is called the fourth pillar of the state because, after the legislature, executive and judiciary, it informs citizens and checks power. This article gives you an outline, a full model essay and exam tips. More study material is on the [Solved Notes](/solved.html) page and in the [books](/books.html) collection.

sections.h2: Media as Teacher, Watchdog and Entertainer
paras: Media teaches us daily: newspapers explain government decisions, television shows documentaries about science and history, and the internet offers lessons, lectures and libraries to students in every village. During examinations, students use educational programmes and online material to revise difficult topics, and farmers learn about weather, crops and markets from radio and television. In this way, media has become a classroom without walls, open day and night to anyone willing to learn.

Media also acts as a watchdog: it reports corruption, injustice and negligence, and forces authorities to answer the public. When a road is broken, a hospital lacks medicine, or an official misuses power, media coverage brings the issue to public attention and often leads to action. At the same time, media entertains: dramas, films, music and sports programmes relax tired minds after work and study. The danger arises when media spreads fake news, exaggerates events for ratings, or fills young minds with useless content, so responsible use of media is as important as media itself.
bullets: Teacher: news, documentaries, online lessons
Watchdog: reports injustice and corruption
Entertainer: dramas, music, sports
Danger: fake news and exaggeration
Responsible use: verify before believing

sections.h2: Essay Outline: Role of Media in Modern Life
paras: Organise this essay by the three roles: teacher, watchdog and entertainer, then a paragraph on dangers and responsible use, ending with a balanced conclusion. This three-roles structure is easy to remember and gives you three strong body paragraphs without repetition. Start by defining media and naming its main forms: newspapers, television, radio and the internet, including social media. Then devote one paragraph to each role with a concrete example, so the examiner sees understanding, not memorised praise.

The dangers paragraph is essential for a high score, because it shows balanced thinking. Mention fake news, the habit of believing every forwarded message, and the waste of time on useless content, then advise readers to verify news from reliable sources before sharing it. End by saying that media, used honestly and wisely, strengthens democracy, knowledge and national unity, while misuse harms all three. A balanced conclusion always scores higher than one that only praises or only criticises.
bullets: Introduction: meaning and forms of media
Body 1: media as teacher
Body 2: media as watchdog
Body 3: media as entertainer
Body 4: dangers and responsible use
Conclusion: honest media, wise readers

diagram.caption: Essay Structure: Role of Media. Follow this order when you write your essay in the examination hall.

sections.h2: Model Essay: Role of Media in Modern Life
paras: Media plays a very important role in modern life, and it includes newspapers, television, radio and the internet, which reach millions of people every day. Media is called the fourth pillar of the state, because it informs citizens, educates society and watches over those in power. In the morning, a newspaper tells us about national and world events; in the evening, television shows news, documentaries and discussions; and at any hour, the internet brings information to our mobile phones within seconds. Without media, people would live in ignorance of their own country and the world, and democracy itself would become weak.

First, media is a great teacher. Students learn from educational programmes, documentaries and online lessons, farmers learn about weather and crops, and citizens learn about their rights, laws and duties. Second, media is a faithful watchdog: it reports corruption, injustice and negligence, and brings public problems to the attention of the government, which often leads to quick action. Third, media is a source of entertainment: dramas, films, music and sports matches relax our minds after hard work and bring families together in the evening. In these three roles, media serves every age group and every section of society.

sections.h2: Model Essay: Conclusion and Useful Vocabulary
paras: However, media also has dangers that we must recognise. Fake news spreads quickly on social media, and many people believe and forward messages without checking their truth, which creates fear, hatred and confusion. Some channels exaggerate events for ratings, and some programmes waste the precious time of students with useless content. The solution is responsible media and wise readers: journalists must report truthfully, and readers must verify news from reliable sources before believing or sharing it. In conclusion, media is a powerful force in modern life, and if it remains honest and its readers remain careful, it will continue to educate, protect and unite our nation.

Useful vocabulary includes: pillar for a main support, democracy for rule by the people, watchdog for one who guards against wrongdoing, and exaggerate for making something seem larger than it is. Use the phrase fourth pillar once, explained simply, rather than repeating it. When writing about social media, be specific: mention forwarded messages and the need to verify, because concrete detail always beats vague warnings in an essay.
bullets: pillar — a main support of a structure
democracy — rule by the people through voting
watchdog — one who guards against wrongdoing
exaggerate — make something seem larger than true
reliable — worthy of trust

sections.h2: Exam Technique for This Essay
paras: Good essays are planned before they are written, and this topic is no exception. Spend the first five minutes making a short outline on the rough-work page: introduction, three or four body points in a sensible order, and a conclusion. This small habit prevents repetition, keeps your ideas in order, and helps you finish on time. In the examination hall, write neatly, leave a clear space between paragraphs, and check your spelling at the end if time allows. A clean, well-organised answer always scores better than a longer, confused one, even when both students know the same facts.

Practise by writing this essay once at home without looking at your notes, then compare your draft with the outline in this article and improve the weak paragraphs. Learn five or six useful words for this topic and use them naturally, not forced into every sentence. Avoid copying long sentences you do not understand, because examiners reward clear, original English. Read your essay aloud once before submitting it in practice: if a sentence sounds strange when spoken, rewrite it in simpler words. With one careful practice essay a week, your speed, confidence and marks will all improve steadily.
bullets: Use the three roles: teacher, watchdog, entertainer
Give one concrete example per role
Add a dangers paragraph for balanced thinking
Advise verifying news before sharing it
End balanced: honest media plus wise readers

points: Media includes newspapers, television, radio and the internet.
As teacher, media spreads knowledge day and night.
As watchdog, media reports injustice and checks power.
Fake news is a real danger of modern media.
Responsible journalists and careful readers together make media useful.

faqs.q: What does fourth pillar of the state mean?
faqs.a: It means media stands beside the legislature, executive and judiciary as a support of democracy. It informs citizens and checks power, so people can vote and act wisely. Explain it in one simple sentence, as in the model essay.

faqs.q: How do I write about social media without being negative only?
faqs.a: Give both sides: social media spreads lessons and news quickly, but also spreads fake news when users forward messages without checking. End with responsible use, which shows balanced and mature thinking.

faqs.q: How long should this essay be in the examination?
faqs.a: For Classes 9 and 10, about 250 to 300 words is a safe length. That is usually five to seven paragraphs: one introduction, three or four body paragraphs and one conclusion. Quality matters more than length, so do not pad your essay with repeated sentences just to make it longer.

faqs.q: Can I change the model essay in my own words?
faqs.a: Yes, and you should. Use the model essay as a guide for structure and ideas, then rewrite it in your own simple English. Examiners reward original writing, so keep the outline, change the examples where you can, and add one personal observation from your own life. You can find more study guides on the [blog](/blog/) page.

title: BIEK Pre-Medical Gazette 2026: How to Read the 178-Page Result Gazette
desc: The BIEK Pre-Medical gazette runs to 178 pages. This guide shows how to find your roll number, read your papers, and act on an Ungraded entry.
kw: BIEK Pre-Medical gazette 2026 178 pages reading guide
intro: A result gazette can look intimidating, especially when it runs to 178 pages, but it is really just a long, organised list, and learning to read it is a useful skill for any BIEK student. The Pre-Medical gazette for HSC Part-I Annual Examination 2026, announced on 26 October 2026, contains the results of thousands of students, arranged so that a roll number can be found if you know how to search rather than flipping page by page. This guide explains how to approach the gazette on biek.edu.pk, what the entries mean in general terms, and what to do if a paper shows Ungraded, without inventing gazette details that are not in the verified snapshot. The verified figures behind the gazette are 25,157 registered, 24,544 appeared, and 11,966 students who passed all six papers, so most readers will be looking for one line among many thousands. Students can also find study support through [solved notes](/solved.html) once they know which papers need work. A gazette rewards patience and method, not speed, and this guide gives you that method.

sections.h2: What a Gazette Is and Where to Find It
paras: A gazette is the board's published result document, listing results in a structured order so that colleges, students, and the public can verify outcomes. Unlike a personal result slip, which shows only your result, a gazette shows many students together, which is why it is long and why it needs a search strategy. For BIEK, results are available on the official website, biek.edu.pk, and through the official BIEK Android app, and the Pre-Medical gazette is reported to run to 178 pages. That length reflects the size of the cohort: with 24,544 students appearing, even a compact listing needs many pages. Do not be put off by the page count; you are not expected to read the gazette from beginning to end, only to locate your own entry accurately.

Start by using the official source only. Unofficial copies of gazettes circulate in chat groups and on file-sharing links, and they may be incomplete, outdated, or altered, even when they look convincing. Download or open the gazette from biek.edu.pk, or use the official app's result view, and keep the official version as your reference. If your college provides a gazette copy, check that it matches the official version before relying on it. A few minutes spent confirming the source can save hours of confusion later, especially if an unofficial copy contains a typographical error in a roll number or a grade. The [books page](/books.html) is a separate study resource and should not be confused with the board's official result documents.

sections.h2: Finding Your Roll Number Without Flipping 178 Pages
paras: The efficient way to find a roll number in a digital gazette is to search, not to browse. If you open the gazette as a document on a computer or phone, use the document's find function and type your full roll number exactly as it appears on your admit card, including any leading zeros or prefixes. Search for the full number rather than part of it, because a partial number can match many other students' numbers and lead you to the wrong line. Once the search lands on a match, check the surrounding entries carefully: confirm that the roll number matches yours digit for digit, and that the name or college details alongside it, if shown, are consistent with your own. If you are using a printed gazette, use the roll-number ordering to narrow the range first, then scan within that range, rather than starting at page one.

Take your time with this step, because a single-digit error can produce a completely different student's result. If the search finds no match, do not immediately assume failure; check for typing errors, check whether you are searching the correct group's gazette, and confirm that your roll number belongs to the Pre-Medical Part-I 2026 gazette announced on 26 October 2026 rather than to another group or year. If the problem persists, ask your college office to help you locate the entry, because colleges work with gazettes regularly and can spot ordering or formatting issues quickly. Never share your roll number in a public group to ask strangers to find your result, because your roll number is personal information and unofficial helpers may return the wrong line.

diagram.alt: Finding Your Gazette Entry in Four Steps
diagram.caption: Search methodically instead of flipping through all 178 pages.

sections.h2: Reading the Columns in General Terms
paras: Gazette entries are laid out in columns or fields so that many results fit on each page, and the exact column headings can vary between boards and years. This guide therefore explains gazette reading in general terms rather than inventing specific Pre-Medical column headings that are not in the verified snapshot. In general, an entry will identify the student by roll number, and will then show an outcome for each paper in the group, followed by an overall outcome. For Pre-Medical Part-I, that means six papers, matching the six-paper structure behind the passed-all-six figure. Read across the entry slowly, paper by paper, and write down each paper's outcome separately, because the overall outcome alone does not tell you which subject needs work if you did not pass all papers.

Pay particular attention to any entry that shows Ungraded, because under the new grading decision, a score under 40 percent in a paper is recorded as Ungraded, meaning not passed in that paper. An Ungraded entry in one paper does not erase passed entries in other papers, and it should be treated as a focused task, not as a whole-result failure. If an entry shows a code, abbreviation, or symbol you do not recognise, do not guess its meaning; ask your teacher or college office to explain it with the gazette in hand. Gazette abbreviations are compact by design, and a wrong guess can lead to a wrong study plan. Keep a written copy of your entry, with the gazette page noted, so that you can refer to it when asking for help.

sections.h2: What to Do If a Paper Shows Ungraded
paras: If your gazette entry shows Ungraded in one or more papers, follow the same calm sequence as for any board result: confirm the entry, tell your parents and teacher, and identify the topics behind the weak paper. A gazette entry is a summary, not a diagnosis, so the next step is to work with your teacher to understand whether the difficulty was conceptual, practised, or related to exam technique in that subject. Pre-Medical subjects build heavily on each other, so a weak paper in Part-I deserves prompt attention before Part-II, even if the overall result feels disappointing. Start re-studying that subject in small daily sessions, using your textbook and class notes, and ask for practice questions in the areas where you lost marks, if your teacher can identify them from your preparation.

On procedures, this guide stays general, because the verified snapshot does not give a general supplementary or rechecking procedure for the 26 October Pre-Medical group, and inventing one would mislead students. Follow the board's own notice on biek.edu.pk for whatever procedure applies to your case, and ask your college which notice is current for Pre-Medical Part-I 2026. Do not follow forwarded messages that claim dates or fees for this group, and do not pay anyone who offers to change a gazette entry, because gazette entries are board records and cannot be changed through unofficial channels. While you wait for any official procedure, your re-study is the part you control, and it is the part that will matter most when the next step opens.
bullets: Confirm the gazette entry digit by digit before acting.
Treat each Ungraded paper as a separate, focused revision task.
Follow only the board's own notice for official procedures.

sections.h2: Using the Gazette Wisely and Safely
paras: A gazette is a public document, but your entry in it should still be handled with care. Do not post your full entry, roll number, or result screenshot in public groups, and do not use another student's entry to compare or to comment on their performance. Colleges and students use gazettes to verify results, not to rank classmates, and the Pre-Medical cohort is large enough that individual comparisons are rarely informative. If you need to prove your result to a college or institution, use the official result or gazette copy through proper channels, and keep your own copy safe for future forms. A gazette entry, once understood, is a tool for planning, not a label to carry in public.

Finally, remember what the gazette does not show. It does not show how hard you worked, which topics you understood deeply, or how much you improved during the year; it shows paper outcomes on one examination occasion. A student who passed all six papers still has weak topics to strengthen for Part-II, and a student with an Ungraded paper still has passed papers and real knowledge to build on. Use the gazette to make a precise study list, then put the gazette aside and return to the textbooks themselves, because that is where improvement actually happens. Students looking for general study methods can explore [study guides](/blog/) alongside their subject revision.

points: The BIEK Pre-Medical Part-I gazette for 2026 runs to 178 pages.
Pre-Medical figures: 25,157 registered, 24,544 appeared, 11,966 passed all six papers.
Search for your full roll number exactly, rather than flipping through the gazette page by page.
Read each of the six papers separately, because Ungraded applies paper by paper.
Follow only the board's own notice on biek.edu.pk for official procedures after an Ungraded paper.

faqs.a: The Pre-Medical gazette is reported to run to 178 pages, reflecting the large cohort of 24,544 appeared students.

faqs.q: Where can I find the official Pre-Medical gazette?
faqs.a: Results are available on the board's official website, biek.edu.pk, and the official BIEK Android app. Use the official source rather than unofficial copies in chat groups.
